messages:
Sam: noticed a spike in TLS client auth failures for `control-plane` in us-east-1 and eu-central around 09:12 UTC. error: `tls: client cert validation failed (kms:Decrypt denied)`
Priya: grabbing logs now. example from sidecar:
```
2026-06-10T09:12:11Z control-plane us-east-1 WARN tls handshake: client auth failed: KMS DecryptDenied keyAlias/control-wrap-2026
```
Diego: looking at infra changes last night PR #5342 removed role binding `keystore-reader` from several service accounts as part of RBAC prune. suspect correlated.
Iris: can we confirm which principal attempted the unwrap? KMS logs only show `principalId` and request id, no cert details to tie to tenant.
Sam: correct. we currently cannot map KMS Deny -> client cert. that's blocking attribution and mitigation choices.
Priya: short-term mitigation: rebind the role to the service account in affected regions or add a scoped KMS allow for `arn:aws:iam::123456:role/keystore-reader-ephemeral` limited to the affected key ARNs for 2 hours. prefer scoped allow.
Diego: i'll open an emergency IAM PR for region-scoped allow with TTL 2h. adding `kms:ViaService` and `aws:RequestedRegion` conditions.
Iris: parallel fix: add minimal cert provenance fields from proxy before KMS call: `client_cert_serial`, `cert_sha256`, `sni`, `handshake_id`. ship behind runtime flag `EMIT_CERT_CONTEXT=true`.
Sam: good. also add `handshake_id` to tracer so we can correlate proxy logs, KMS audit, and traces.
Priya: alert rule suggestion: if `client_handshake_fail_rate > 3%` AND `kms:Decrypt_deny > 0.5%` for 5m, page sec-oncall.
Diego: deployed emergency IAM allow in us-east-1. DeployBot: deploy success for `keystore-temp-allow` by @Diego.
AuditBot: ticket created: TICKET-2026-81100 High Multi-region keystore unwrap denies causing mTLS failures.
Iris: forensics note: after hotfix we should run handshake replays from synthetic clients with known cert fingerprints and verify KMS audit entries include `handshake_id` so we can map denies.
Sam: long-term idea: reduce KMS unwrap on the critical path by using region-local wrapping keys and cached unwrap tokens, or adopt an on-host asymmetric wrap so proxies don't call KMS per-handshake. Diego, can you own a design spike?
Diego: yes. will propose options: envelope-with-local-wrapping, short-lived session keys, or signed provenance tokens.
Priya: CI additions: 1) RBAC prune dry-run that validates keystore access for all critical services, 2) handshake smoke after IAM changes, 3) audit correlation assertion (handshake_id present).
Iris: will land the hotfix to emit cert context now and attach sample log lines to the ticket. tagging sec-oncall @Priya.
Sam: thanks. keep this thread updated with canary results. closing emergency channel when failure rate normal <1% for 10m. :white_check_mark:
